parsedVerdict.reasoning: An application-layer use case should load aggregates, call domain behaviour, save the results and map them to DTOs. CancelOrderUseCase.execute does more than that. It contains the order state-transition rule, deciding which states can be cancelled and throwing InvalidStateTransitionError. It changes order.state and order.updatedAt directly. It also changes product.stock directly to put reserved stock back. These are business rules and aggregate invariants, so they belong in the domain layer (for example order.cancel() or product.restock(), or OrderDomainService). Keeping them in the use case leaves the domain model anemic. The rest of the file fits the application layer: fetching through repository ports, calling the domain service to release reservations, saving, and mapping to an OrderResponse DTO.

violations.message: CancelOrderUseCase.execute contains the order cancellation rule (it rejects cancellation when state is 'shipped' or 'delivered' and throws InvalidStateTransitionError) and sets order.state = 'cancelled' and order.updatedAt directly. This business rule and state transition belong in the domain layer, for example an Order.cancel() method.

CancelOrderUseCase.execute changes inventory directly with `product.stock += reservation.quantity`. Restoring stock is domain logic and belongs in the domain layer (a Product method or a domain service), not in the application use case.
